note: oam@1: for each of the 1 197 CBSE (NCERT) and Tamil Nadu State Board outcomes (content/learning/syllabus), which question families, written tasks and authored questions really assess it, and whether every part of the statement is assessed at its level (full), only part (partial, with what is missing) or nothing (none). Judged from the content itself — sampled problems of every family of the mapped competencies — by AI assessors working to a written brief, after an independent audit found that mapping alone overclaimed. Provisional: not educator-reviewed. The coverage compiler calls an outcome engineering-complete only where this map says full and fit.
judgedAgainst: the modules as they draw on every family of their competency (pools@1), the written tasks (written@2) and authored questions, at commit 2276be0

outcomes.missing: Only left/right in a row (aarow) and just above/below on shelves (aashelf) are asked; inside/outside, near/far and in front of/behind are not assessed.
Comparing objects or groups by sight (big/small, more/fewer) without counting is not asked; the mapped families compare written numerals.
Naming/recognising solids is asked (aasolid); sorting objects into round and flat-faced groups is not (that is abroll, in a competency not mapped here).
Sides and corners are counted (abside), but telling straight from curved sides is never asked (a circle only appears as a shape with 0 sides).
Which is more/less is asked, but the 'equal' case is never asked (aacmp always gives two different numbers), and comparing groups is not in the mapped families.
Just before/just after is asked (aanext); putting single-digit numbers (up to 9) in order is not, since aaordn only orders two-digit numbers.
acstory numbers start at 12, so no story within 9 is asked; making up one's own number story is not assessed (wr:op-stories is Grade 4 and asks for a multiplication story).
Only sums and differences within 20 are asked as bare number sentences; two-digit numbers beyond 20 without regrouping (e.g. 34 + 25) and everyday-context problems are not assessed.
Naming the days of the week and the months in order is not asked; the calendar families ask dates of weekdays and day counts.
An amount is made only one way (one note/coin plus coins of one kind); making the same amount with different combinations is not asked.
'Is it enough / how much more' is asked (abneed, always a not-enough case); the total cost of two items is not asked.
Numbers are read from blocks that are already grouped into tens; grouping a loose collection into tens to count it is not asked.
Only the value of the tens digit is asked (aadigit); the value of the ones digit is not, and writing numerals is only typing the answer.
Cubes, cylinders, cones and spheres are asked; cuboids are never asked for (aasolid limits).
Rectangles are never identified (aaflat) or counted (abside); only circles, triangles and squares (plus pentagons/hexagons).
Straight vs curved is asked only for capital letters; lines in pictures and objects are not assessed.
Only additions that need regrouping are asked; two-digit addition without regrouping is not.
Only subtractions that need regrouping are asked; two-digit subtraction without regrouping is not.
Measuring a length in units is asked (aaclip); comparing two lengths measured in non-standard units is not.
Comparing (most/least, how many more cups) is asked; ordering containers by how much they hold is not.
The total of equal groups is found, but writing it as a repeated addition (or matching multiplication) sentence is not asked.
Days, dates and weeks on a calendar are asked; relating months to seasons is not.
The four directions (north, south, east, west) are never asked; abgrid/abmove use left/right/up/down only, and wr:map-route is a Grade 4 route task.
Number names are turned into numerals (aaword); writing numbers in words is not assessed (no written task asks for it).
Comparing and ordering is asked only up to 99; numbers 100 to 200 are not compared or ordered.
addr stops at totals of 99 and adcol3 adds two three-digit numbers (totals mostly over 200), so totals from 100 to 200 are hardly ever asked.
Triangles and squares in different orientations are asked; rectangles are never asked for.
Sides and corners are counted; diagonals are not, and sorting shapes by these properties is not asked.
Joining points with straight lines to make a triangle and a rectangle is asked; making shapes by paper folding and cutting cannot be done or assessed in the app.
Comparing and ordering is asked only up to 99; numbers 100 to 500 are not compared or ordered.
The total of equal groups is found, but describing/writing it as repeated addition is not asked.
Equal sharing and grouping are asked (acshare); division by repeated subtraction is not.
Naming halves and quarters of a grid is asked; checking whether the parts are equal (shapes cut into unequal parts) is not.
Comparing 1/2 and 1/4 as fractions is asked (a few adfcmp items); comparing them on a number line is not.
Comparing and ordering is asked only up to 99; three-digit numbers up to 1000 are not compared or ordered.
Measuring in whole centimetres on a ruler is asked; measuring in metres (tape) is not.
Estimating a short length and checking it with a ruler is asked (wr:len-ruler); choosing a suitable unit and tool, and estimating distances, are not. adest (rounding sums) is unrelated.
Estimating capacity and checking it is asked (wr:est-capacity); estimating weight and word problems about weight and capacity are not. adest (rounding sums) is unrelated.
Only additions that need regrouping are asked; two- and three-digit addition without regrouping is not.
Only subtractions that need regrouping are asked; two- and three-digit subtraction without regrouping is not.
Seconds, minutes and hours are related; days and months (hours in a day, days in a month) are not.
Classifying solids by their properties, and faces/edges/corners of curved solids (cylinder, cone, sphere); flat versus curved surfaces is tested only indirectly through 'can it roll or slide'.
Identifying right angles in pictures of objects and figures (angles are given only as degree numbers); checking with a folded-paper right-angle tool is hands-on and not done in the app.
Identifying the centre, a radius and a diameter in a circle; only the radius-diameter calculation is asked.
Matching given top/front/side views to objects or block buildings, and side views; the written task only asks to draw a front and a top view (aisolid counts faces of prisms, which is unrelated).
Describing a seat in a 2-D seating layout by its row and column; only ordinal places in a single row (Grade 1 level) and grid coordinates after moves are asked.
Classifying by pairing (objects or dots put in pairs); only the last-digit method on written numbers is tested.
Showing the same amount in two or more different ways, with mixed notes and coins; aamake uses one note plus coins of a single kind and asks only how many coins.
Reading and writing four-digit number names in words, and writing a number in expanded form (only expanded form or blocks to numeral is asked).
Regrouping (for example 14 tens as 1 hundred 4 tens); the block pictures always show at most 9 of each kind.
Comparing four-digit numbers by where they lie on a number line; only reading the number at a marked position is asked.
Writing comparisons with the < and > signs, and descending order; aecmp asks only for ascending order (aacmp/aaordn are two-digit, Grade 1 level).
Dividing shapes into halves in several ways; the drawing task asks only for quarters.
Explaining why more sharers give smaller shares; unit fractions are only named from shaded grids and compared.
Recognising equal fractions from folded or partitioned pictures; only symbolic missing-numerator questions are asked and folding paper is hands-on.
Estimating lengths in metres, half metres and quarter metres; only a centimetre guess-and-check is asked, and real measuring is hands-on.
Comparing lengths written in m and cm.
Checking the answer by estimating (no estimation family is mapped), and adding a two-digit number to a three-digit number.
Using an estimate to check a computed subtraction; estimation is asked separately and only for two-digit numbers rounded to tens.
Number-placement puzzles (placing digits or numbers in a grid).
The learner making their own estimate of a weight; the written task only discusses checking someone else's guess, and real weighing is hands-on.
Writing a multiplication as repeated addition (or the reverse); the learner only finds the total of a pictured array.
Relating division to multiplication (for example writing the multiplication fact behind a division).
Four-digit numbers (adcol3 stops at sums of 999) and word-problem contexts.
Four-digit numbers (adcol3 is three-digit only) and finding increases and decreases in context.
Patterns in an addition chart and in reverse-and-add sums; only the parity of odd + odd is asked.
Lines of symmetry in designs and in shapes other than a square; the automatic questions ask only whether capital letters have a vertical or a horizontal line.
Predicting fold-and-cut designs.
Describing or drawing the mirror images of letters, digits and words; only whether letters have a line of symmetry is asked.
Number of days in each month, identifying leap years, writing dates as DD/MM/YYYY, and finding ages.
Durations in hours and minutes; acelapsed asks only for 5 to 90 minutes, answered in minutes.
Reading the clock to the exact minute (only 5-minute times), and relating half and quarter hours to minutes.
Building tables beyond 12 (such as x14, x15) by splitting, doubling and halving known facts; mul only asks recall up to 12 x 12.
Two-digit x two-digit multiplication and the partial-products method; mmul is two-digit x one-digit only.
Finding totals across a pictograph (excluded from acpictmore), and reading and completing tables.
Interpreting 'only one', 'both' and 'neither' categories; adtwo asks only for a missing cell in a 2 x 2 table.
Writing numbers in words, and placing Indian commas; only words to figures (without commas) is asked.
Estimating large quantities (thousands and more) in real contexts such as travel distances; adest rounds two-digit numbers only.
Crossing (river-crossing type) logic puzzles.
Shading or drawing a fraction on a grid, and recognising that the same fraction looks different in different wholes.
Placing fractions greater than 1 on a number line.
Measuring a given turn or angle in eighths with the paper tool; the written task asks only to draw given eighths, and making the tool is hands-on (afprot reads a degree protractor instead).
Naming the compass direction faced after a given turn; afturn gives both directions and asks only for the fraction of a turn.
Four- and five-digit numbers; adcol3 is three-digit only.
Writing related addition/subtraction facts and checking an answer with the inverse operation; acmissing only fills a box, with numbers up to 40.
Mental shortcuts: complements to 100, 1000 and 10000, and subtracting 9 or 99; adcol3 tests written column addition and subtraction.
Sums of consecutive numbers, and the parity of even + even and even + odd.
Choosing a suitable unit (mm, cm, m or km); ablen only reads whole centimetres on a ruler.
Millimetres, and kilometres from metres (km-m is asked only from large to small).
Measuring to the nearest millimetre (only whole centimetres), and drawing segments of given lengths.
Dividing lengths given in mixed units.
Estimating heights and distances from reference lengths, and relating feet and inches to centimetres.
Doubling, halving and nearest-multiple strategies for products; mul only asks recall of facts.
Multi-digit x multi-digit multiplication (for example 3-digit x 2-digit) and the partial-products method; mmul is two-digit x one-digit only.
Grade-level work: only short number or shape repeats (Grade 1 level) are asked, not weaving patterns described and extended as ordered sequences.
Kites (excluded from afquad).
Matching views of cubes and solids, and matching nets in the automatic questions (cube nets appear only in a drawing task).
Judging whether a recorded weight is sensible and choosing between mg, g and kg; abkg only reads a balance.
Milligrams, grams to kilograms, and comparing weights with <, = and >.
Dividing weights given in mixed units.
Writing the division facts for a given multiplication fact, and stating dividend = divisor x quotient.
Dividing multiples of 10, 100 and 1000 by other numbers (for example 2400 / 6); only division by 10, 100 and 1000 is asked.
The mental strategies (splitting the dividend, halving repeatedly); only the quotient is asked.
Long division of larger numbers that leaves a remainder (remainders only for two-digit dividends), and checking with N = D x Q + R.
Tables of quantities and costs with missing values to work out.
Lines of symmetry in digits and numbers; only capital letters are asked.
Estimating the area of irregular shapes, and comparing the areas of two shapes; only whole rectangles on a grid are counted.
Comparing race times, and choosing seconds or minutes for an activity.
Adding time durations, and changing seconds back to minutes and seconds.
Sorting numbers by divisibility by 2, 5 and 10; akdivd asks for missing digits for divisibility by 3, 9, 11 and 6.
Estimating distances on a map (for example with a scale).
Judging given statements about a picture or graph as true or false; the questions only ask for readings and differences.
Stating the rule that generates each sequence is not asked: affig/abseq only ask for a later term (squares, triangular, cube, doubling, odd, skip counting).
Naming the vertex and arms of an angle, and comparing two angles (by superposition or rotation), are not assessed; only the size of a clock-face turn is.

Drawing an angle of a given size with a protractor is not assessed (the written task draws grid angles without a protractor); measuring is only reading a protractor described in words, not measuring a drawn angle.
Reflex angles are never classified (aeang uses acute/right/obtuse/straight only); classifying from drawings is only the Grade 4 drawing task.
Digit-sum explorations are not assessed, and no conjecture about Kaprekar's routine (e.g. reaching 6174) is formed or tested: akkap is a single step.
Describing the behaviour of Collatz sequences (e.g. that they reach 1 and loop) is not assessed; only individual terms are generated.
Only rounding-then-adding/subtracting of 2- and 3-digit numbers; mental-calculation strategies and judging the size of quantities and results are not assessed.
No clock or calendar number patterns: acelapsed only finds durations in minutes.
Collecting data for a question cannot be done in the app; the tally/frequency table itself is only marked in the (Grade 9) written task, the automatic questions mark a count read from it.
Reading pictographs with partial symbols is not assessed (acpict uses whole pictures only); automatic reading is at Grade 2-3 level. Drawing is covered by wr:pg-books.
No question asks whether two numbers are co-prime (aghcf3 always has HCF at least 2; aglcm only finds an LCM).
Using the prime factorisation to check divisibility and co-primeness is not assessed (ajsqm uses it only for perfect squares).
Perimeter of a square or regular polygon from one side (4 x side, n x side) is never asked: every side is marked and simply added (Grade 3-4 level).
Estimating the area of irregular shapes by counting squares is not assessed (aearea uses whole rectangles only).
Using fractional units to measure lengths is not assessed; only shaded parts of grids and building from unit fractions.
Reducing a fraction to its lowest terms is not assessed; eqfrac only scales up to a missing numerator.

Fractions with different numerators AND denominators are never compared or ordered automatically (only common top or bottom); ordering unlike fractions is not assessed at all; the written task compares two by benchmarks only.
Subtraction of fractions, addition with like denominators, and word problems are not assessed; faddu only adds two unlike fractions.
Representing integers on a number line (e.g. floors above/below ground) is not assessed; only ordering lists of integers.

Reading/writing numbers in crores, comparing numbers in lakhs and crores, converting millions/billions back to the Indian system, and billions are not assessed; aeind stops at 9,99,999 and aecmp at five digits.
Deciding when an exact value is needed and when an estimate is enough is not assessed, and rounding stops at 9,999 (no large numbers in lakhs/crores).
mmul is only two-digit x one-digit multiplication; nothing uses patterns with powers of ten or estimates large products/quantities.
Writing an arithmetic expression for a situation is not assessed; agbod only evaluates given expressions.
Identifying the terms of an expression is not assessed; only evaluation with brackets.
Comparing two expressions without evaluating them is not assessed; the automatic questions mark only the final value, so the rewriting itself is checked only in the written task.
Thousandths are not used and the place value of a given digit is never asked; aedec is ones/tenths/hundredths blocks (Grade 4 level).
Writing a measurement in the larger unit as a decimal (e.g. 245 cm = 2.45 m, 750 g = 0.75 kg) is never asked; conversions are whole-number, mostly to the smaller unit.
Ordering several decimals is not assessed (aedecc compares two numbers only).
Measurement problems and word problems are not assessed; money appears only as bare rupee sums.

Identifying parallel/perpendicular lines in a given figure is not assessed, and making parallel lines by folding is not asked (the written task describes only perpendicular creases); paper folding itself cannot be done in the app.
Naming/identifying corresponding and alternate angles in a figure is not assessed: every question states which pair it is, and there is no figure.
Linking Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers to counting problems (rhythms of short and long beats) and exploring their patterns are not assessed; only terms are generated.
Interpreting a fraction product with an area model is not assessed; only the calculation.
Dividing a whole number by a fraction (e.g. 6 / (3/4)) is not asked; aifdiv divides fractions by fractions or by whole numbers only.
Word problems are not assessed: fraction products and quotients are bare calculations, and acstory is whole-number one-step stories (Grade 2).
Recognising congruent figures (deciding which shapes are congruent) is not assessed; only reading corresponding parts from a congruence statement.
Expressions that combine several integer operations, and context problems that need multiplication, are not assessed; each question is a single operation on two integers.
LCM of three or more numbers is not assessed; aglcm uses two numbers only.
Word problems (grouping, scheduling) are not assessed; HCF and LCM are bare calculations.
Nothing estimates decimal products or quotients, and there are no context problems; adest only rounds two-digit whole numbers.
Telling statistical questions apart from other questions and from statements (classifying given items) is not asked; the task states that the questions are not statistical and asks for rewrites.
Writing an equation to model a situation or puzzle is not asked: lin gives the equation, meet is trial of x^2 = ax + b, and the written task corrects given solutions.
Forming the equation from a word problem is not assessed; lin only solves given equations ax + b = c.
Possible last digits of perfect squares, and deciding whether a given number is a perfect square, are not asked; only sums of consecutive odd numbers and counts between consecutive squares are.
Numbers that are sums of two cubes in two ways (e.g. 1729) are not asked; only cubes as sums of consecutive odd numbers (written) and the odd-number pattern for squares.
Writing a repeated multiplication (e.g. 3 x 3 x 3 x 3) in exponential notation is not asked; pow only evaluates given powers.
Comparing quantities written in scientific notation is not asked (the family limits say comparing is separate).
Nothing asks for an order-of-magnitude estimate of a real-world quantity or a plausibility judgement; aksci/akscid only convert exact numbers, and adest is Grade 3 rounding of 2-digit sums.
Only Roman numerals are asked about; other early systems (e.g. tally, Egyptian, Babylonian, Mayan) and how they recorded numbers are not.
Unknown SIDES of parallelograms and rhombuses (opposite sides equal, all rhombus sides equal) are not asked; only angles and diagonal lengths.
Kites are not included (afquad limits); identifying a kite by its properties is not assessed. Trapeziums appear only as isosceles trapeziums.
Only Grade 3-5 level: plain division remainders and factor lists. Grade 8 reasoning about remainders (remainders of sums/products, numbers leaving a given remainder) is not asked.
Only two-digit additions with one hidden digit per number (about Grade 6 level); multi-letter cryptarithms and multiplication puzzles of the chapter are not asked.

No automatic question uses (a+b)^2, (a-b)^2 or (a+b)(a-b): family expand is only (x+a)(x+b) with a != b (checked: no squares or a^2-b^2 cases). Only one written item expands (x+5)^2; expanding with (a-b)^2 and (a+b)(a-b) is not asked.
Deciding whether two given ratios are equivalent is not asked (ajeqr only fills a missing term).

Only Grade 4 metric conversions (m-cm, kg-g, L-mL); conversion with a conversion factor (e.g. inches-cm, km/h-m/s, currency) by proportional reasoning is not asked. Unit-rate families do not convert units.
Only hundredths <-> percent and percent -> decimal (Grade 5 level); percent -> fraction, fraction <-> decimal and fractions like 3/8 are not asked.
Finding what percentage one quantity is of another is not asked; pct only finds a percentage of an amount.
Generating Pythagorean triples (by a rule) or checking whether three numbers form one is not asked; ahpyth only finds a missing side of a whole-number right triangle.
The converse (deciding whether a triangle is right-angled) and real-life contexts are not asked; ahpyth is bare triangles only (2 prompt shapes).

Recognising whether two quantities are in inverse proportion is not asked (ahinv states it), and ahinv is abstract x/y only; workers-and-time inverse-proportion problems are not asked (ahwork is combined work rates).
The mean as a balance point (deviations balancing) is not asked; computing and predicting changes are (written).
No question gives the mean and asks for a missing value; mean4 only computes the mean of four numbers (one prompt shape).
The median of data given in a frequency table is not asked; akmed uses raw lists only.
Building a display with a spreadsheet, actually building (not describing) an infographic, and telling a story with data are not assessed.
Calendar and grid patterns are not included (ahpyr limits); only number pyramids.
Splitting a polygon into triangles (and trapeziums) is not asked; only L-shapes from rectangles and rectangular paths.
Using a grid to describe a floor plan or map is not asked.
Mapped families alpmul/alpdiv multiply and divide polynomials; nothing asks to recognise polynomials, name terms/coefficients/degree or classify linear polynomials.
Linear decay (steady decrease) situations are not modelled; only one written growth context (stamps), and alrule is context-free.
Classifying numbers as natural/whole/integer/rational, placing rationals on the number line and absolute values are not asked; only picking out the irrational number.
Exploring cyclic patterns in recurring expansions (e.g. multiples of 1/7) is not asked.
Historical approaches such as Madhava's series are not asked, and why pi is irrational is only touched via 22/7 != pi.
(a+b+c)^2 and the cube identities are not asked; expand is only (x+a)(x+b).

Family factor is only monic x^2+px+q with distinct roots (checked: no perfect squares, no difference of squares); none of the named identity factorisations (a^2-b^2, perfect squares, sum/difference of cubes, a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc) is asked.
Non-monic trinomials ax^2+bx+c (splitting the middle term) are not asked, and the algebra-tile stage cannot be done in the app; only monic x^2+px+q.
Arc, segment and sector vocabulary and the symmetries of a circle are not asked; aecirc is Grade 4 radius/diameter.
Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre (and converse) is neither proved nor applied; the converse of the perpendicular-bisects-chord theorem is not asked.
The converse (chords equidistant from the centre are equal) and 'the longer chord is nearer the centre' are not asked.
The written proof deduces the semicircle angle but not that angles in the same segment are equal (that fact is only applied in altheo).
Deciding whether four points are concyclic and the converse (supplementary opposite angles => cyclic) are not asked.
Explaining that C/d is the same constant pi and recalling historical approximations are not asked; polygon perimeters only as Grade 4 rectangles.
The perimeter of a sector is not asked in the mapped families (sector perimeter sits in aisector, competency circle-area, not mapped here).
Area of a parallelogram is not asked by the mapped families; rectangles only at Grade 5 level.
Deriving the area of a circle is not asked; only using the formulas.
Describing randomness and placing events on the scale in words (likely/unlikely) are not asked; akchance computes Grade 6 bag probabilities (including 0 and 1).
Listing a sample space and describing events as subsets are not asked; akss only counts outcomes.
Only Grade 3-4 add-the-same-amount patterns; Grade 9 sequences (non-linear, multiplicative, mixed) are not asked.
Converting an explicit rule to a recursive rule, and generating terms from an explicit rule, are not asked; only recursive -> terms and arithmetic recursive -> explicit.
Identifying whether a sequence is an AP, and relating an AP to a linear graph or everyday contexts, are not asked; only the nth term.
Identifying whether a sequence is a GP and GP growth/decay in context are not asked; only nth term and sums of given GPs.
Saying when an average of averages misleads is not asked; only computing the combined mean.
Concentration or price of a mixture is not asked (anwmean limits exclude mixtures); pct is a plain percentage of an amount.
Testing divisors only up to the square root, primality of a larger number and step-by-step prime factorisation are not asked; only Grade 5 factor lists and primes up to 100.
Euclid's subtraction algorithm and Aryabhata's division method are not asked in the mapped content; hcf checks only the HCF value.
Defining a 4-gon and telling convex from non-convex quadrilaterals are not asked; only the 360-degree sum.
The proof that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other is not asked in the mapped competency (it is wr:tpf:diagonals, competency triangle-proof).
Proving the converse tests (both pairs of opposite sides equal, opposite angles equal, diagonals bisect => parallelogram) is not asked; only the one-pair-equal-and-parallel test is proved.
The converse of the midpoint theorem is only stated, never proved or applied; ammid applies the theorem to lengths only.
Recognising that a linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions is not asked.
Only the solution is checked; solving by substitution AND by elimination as named methods is not required (the written task asks for either one).
Surface area is asked only for square-based pyramids; other polygonal bases are not.

Stating the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (uniqueness) is never asked; no automatic question asks for a prime factorisation (hcf only asks the HCF of two numbers up to 100, agprime only lists primes).
Word problems with HCF/LCM are not assessed; no automatic LCM questions or use of HCF x LCM = product to find an unknown (only checked once in a written task); hcf is HCF of two numbers up to 100.
Reading the number of zeros from a graph: no family shows a graph (alsym/alform/alpmul/alpdiv are algebraic).
Checking the sum and product of the zeros against the coefficients is never asked; factorising is only the Grade-8 box form (x - a)(x + [ ]) of monic x^2 + px + q, no non-monic quadratics.
Finding unknown coefficients from conditions on the zeros is not assessed.
Finding parameter values for a given case (one/none/infinitely many) is not assessed (alcons limits say so).
Substitution itself is not assessed: alsys/alsysw are answer-only: the named method itself is never required or seen; the written task lets the learner choose substitution or elimination.
Elimination itself is not assessed: alsys/alsysw are answer-only: the named method itself is never required or seen; the written task lets the learner choose substitution or elimination.
Only money (shopping/ticket) contexts; ages, speeds, digits and geometry problems are not assessed.

Recognising whether an equation is quadratic / writing it in standard form, and forming quadratics from situations: the mapped content (quad, wr:quad:graph-k) only solves or sketches given quadratics.
Only monic x^2 + bx + c with whole-number roots; equations with leading coefficient other than 1 (genuine splitting of the middle term) are not assessed.
Quadratic formula is never needed: quad has only monic equations with whole-number roots; no irrational or fractional roots.
Finding parameter values for equal or real roots is not assessed (disc only asks how many real solutions).
Only rectangle-area contexts; speed, age and number problems are not assessed.
Deciding whether a list is an AP is not assessed; apn always states it is an AP (a and d are used, not asked).
Deriving the nth-term formula, the nth term from the end, and finding which term has a given value are not assessed; apn only asks term number n.
Everyday problems (savings, instalments, arrangements) and sums in context are not assessed; apn is a bare nth-term question.
The converse of the BPT (showing lines are parallel) is not assessed.
Applying the AA/SSS/SAS criteria (similarity is always given in amsim) and finding unknown angles are not assessed.
Testing collinearity and classifying triangles by distances are not assessed by the mapped content (anpts does this but belongs to MATH.reasoning.mathematical-argument, not mapped here).
Section formula (internal division, midpoint, trisection): cdist only asks the distance between two points.
Finding the ratio of division and unknown vertices with the section formula: cdist only asks distances.
Justifying (deriving) the values of the ratios at 30, 45, 60 degrees is not asked; only evaluation of expressions.
Telling tangents, secants and non-intersecting lines apart (classifying a given line) is not asked; only the number of tangents from a point.
Only clock-hand contexts; wipers, designs and other figures combining sectors and segments are not assessed.
Only cylinder/cone/hemisphere combinations; solids involving a cube, cuboid or sphere are not assessed.
Only cylinder/cone/hemisphere combinations; solids involving a cube, cuboid or sphere are not assessed.
The prompts already name the component solids (the learner never models the object); tents (open shapes) and vessels are left out.
The assumed-mean and step-deviation methods are not assessed: angmean is answer-only: the named method itself is never required or seen.
Recognising impossible and sure events and giving their probabilities 0 and 1 is not asked directly.
Classifying sets as empty, finite, infinite or equal, and writing a roster set in set-builder form (aosetop only turns set-builder into a list).
Identifying whether a given set is a subset/proper subset and writing out the power set; only the counts are asked.
Reading an interval off a given number-line picture (number lines are only drawn, from inequalities).
Practical (word-problem) counting situations; aoinex gives n(A), n(B), ... directly with no context.
Writing out the ordered pairs of A × B (or A × B × C) from given sets, and equality of ordered pairs; only counting and reading sets back from a product are asked.
Deciding whether a relation is a function (nothing in the mapped competency asks it); ranges are only of quadratics.
Graphs of rational (1/x), signum, exponential and logarithmic functions, and of identity/polynomials beyond y = x³; reading/interpreting these graphs.
Sum, difference, product and quotient of functions and the domain of the result; the mapped families only compose functions.
The unit-circle definition and arguments given as real numbers (radians); atval uses degree multiples of 30°/45° and tests quadrant signs only implicitly.
Domain and range of the six functions (only y = 3 cos 2x in the written task) and sketches of sin, tan, cot, sec and cosec.
Simplifying trigonometric expressions with the sum/difference formulas; only exact values are asked.
A proof using double-angle (and product-to-sum) formulas; the written proofs use sum-to-product and triple-angle only, double-angle/product-to-sum are only computed or recognised.
Addition/subtraction and the multiplicative inverse 1/z; ascop multiplies and divides complex numbers only.
Finding the conjugate and using conjugate properties (the conjugate is only plotted once in the written task).
Systems of two or more linear inequalities in one variable; lineq is single inequalities and the only double inequality is one written task.
